## Resistor power at 143% — actually fine for true accidental contact

Thick-film and thin-film SMD resistor arrays have well-characterized overload tolerance curves. For typical chip resistors at 143% of rated:

| Duration | Verdict |
|---|---|
| < 1 second (true accidental touch) | **No concern.** Most arrays handle 5-10× rated power for 1 second. |

Important data point: your real-world test maxes out at 3.5M counts/sec. So **8M is a spec-sheet number for marketing parity, not a use-case requirement**. That changes how much you should pay for it.

Worth checking before you commit either way: **you don't have to pick between 10k/18k and 20k/36k.** Intermediate values exist and one of them might give you 8M without the worst trade-offs of either extreme.
